mainTopic: Wartime wine, craftsmen paid with יין נסך, the wine tax, and when a גוי acquires wine bought from a Jew
overview: This amud opens with a contradiction. The previous משנה said soldiers at war have no time to pour wine for עבודה זרה, yet a משנה in כתובות forbids all the כהנות in a captured city because soldiers may have violated them. רב מרי answers that pouring libations needs leisure, but lust acts even in a rush. A new משנה follows: Jewish craftsmen whom a גוי pays with a barrel of יין נסך may ask for its value in money, but only before the barrel enters their possession. רב then permits a Jew to ask a גוי to settle the king's wine tax for him. A ברייתא forbids saying 'go in my place,' but רב shows his case matches the ברייתא's permitted line, 'save me from the tax collector.' Another משנה rules that when a Jew sells wine to a גוי, the money is permitted if the price was set before the wine was measured out, and forbidden if it was measured first. אמימר and רב אשי argue about whether משיכה acquires for a גוי. רב אשי brings support from רב's advice to wine sellers to take payment before measuring. His proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Contradiction: soldiers do have time to sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous משנה's idea that soldiers at war have no free time to sin. Another משנה forbids all the כהנות in a captured city, which assumes soldiers do have time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction: A city that was captured by a siege army, all the כהנות in it are disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one משנה against another. Our משנה assumes soldiers are too busy to sin, but a משנה in כתובות assumes they are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה said that when troops enter a city in wartime, the open wine stays permitted, because soldiers have no free time to pour it for עבודה זרה. But the משנה in כתובות says every כהנת in a conquered city becomes forbidden to her husband, because we fear the soldiers violated her. If soldiers have time for that, why not also for pouring wine?

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: one source is set against another
Siege troops, an army laying siege to a city

phrases.english: Gemara: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: This is aimed at the last משנה, which said soldiers in wartime have no time to pour wine for idols.

phrases.english: A city that was captured by a siege army —
all the כהנות in it are disqualified!
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כתובות 27a; the worry is that the soldiers violated them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the previous משנה about troops in wartime
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that soldiers in wartime have no free time to commit sins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in כתובות forbids the כהנות of a captured city, which shows that soldiers do have time to sin even during war.

steps.title: No time to pour wine, but time for lust
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי explains that pouring libations takes free time, while immoral acts happen even in a rush.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: To pour libations there is no time; to have relations there is time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the contradiction by separating the two kinds of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring wine for עבודה זרה is something soldiers do calmly, when they are at ease, so in the middle of a war they skip it. Lust is a strong urge that acts even in a hurry, so we must fear for the women. The two משניות do not contradict, because they deal with different desires.

keyTerms.meaning: To pour wine as a libation for עבודה זרה

steps.whatToRemember: Soldiers at war are not assumed to pour wine for idols, so the wine stays permitted. But the כהנות in a captured city are forbidden, because lust works even in a rush.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
To pour libations there is no time,
to have relations there is time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases: different desires behave differently under wartime pressure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Soldiers either have time for all sins or for none.
steps.terutzMaskana: Soldiers lack time for calm acts like pouring libations, but lust acts even in a hurry.

steps.title: Craftsmen paid with libation wine
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: Jewish craftsmen whom a גוי sent יין נסך as wages may ask for its money value instead, but not once the barrel is already in their possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: Jewish craftsmen to whom a גוי sent a barrel of יין נסך as their wages may say, 'Give us its value.' Once it entered their possession, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule about getting paid with forbidden wine, and the timing makes the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the barrel is theirs, the craftsmen are simply asking for their wages in money, and they never owned the forbidden wine. Once the barrel is in their possession, trading it back for money would be like selling יין נסך, and that counts as getting הנאה from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured for עבודה זרה, forbidden even for benefit

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether they may drink the wine, which is clearly forbidden. It is whether they may take money in its place, and that depends on whether the wine already became theirs.

phrases.english: Mishnah: Jewish craftsmen
to whom a gentile sent
a barrel of libation wine as their wages —
it is permitted to say: "Give us its value";
once it has entered their possession, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה, a new topic about getting paid with forbidden wine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Craftsmen may ask for money instead of יין נסך before it enters their possession, but not afterward.

steps.title: Asking a gentile to handle the king's tax
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a Jew may ask a גוי to go and settle the government tax for him, even if the גוי pays it with יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person may say to a גוי, 'Go and appease the king's tax collectors for me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's ruling about a related money situation: getting a גוי to take care of a tax for you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jew only asks the גוי to free him from the tax and will repay him afterward. How the גוי pays, even with יין נסך, is the גוי's own business, so the Jew is not seen as using the forbidden wine.

keyTerms.meaning: The king's portion, the government tax (here on wine)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Gemara: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is permitted for a person to say to a gentile:
"Go and appease the king's portion for me."
phrases.notes: He is telling the גוי to settle the government wine tax for him, even if the גוי pays with forbidden wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ruling about benefiting indirectly from forbidden wine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may ask a גוי to settle the king's tax for him.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to forbid it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a person may not tell a גוי 'go in my place to the tax collector,' which seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: A person may not say to a גוי, 'Go in my place to the tax collector.'
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges רב with a ברייתא that seems to forbid exactly what he permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases involve a Jew sending a גוי to deal with the wine tax for him. If the ברייתא forbids it, רב's permission seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Go in my place, in my stead
The tax collector or commissary who collects the wine tax

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A person may not say to a gentile:
"Go in my place to the tax collector."

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's permission to ask a גוי to settle the king's tax
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids sending a גוי to the tax collector for you, which looks like the same case.

steps.title: 'In my place' is different from 'save me'
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that 'go in my place' is not his case. His case matches the ברייתא's permitted line, 'save me from the tax collector.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: You are comparing it to 'Go in my place to the tax collector'? My case is only like this other one: but he may say to him, 'Save me from the tax collector.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends his ruling by showing the ברייתא itself has two cases, and his case matches the permitted one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'in my place' makes the גוי the Jew's agent, so whatever the גוי pays counts as if the Jew paid it with יין נסך. Saying 'save me' only asks the גוי to get the Jew out of the obligation. Whatever the גוי pays is his own doing, and רב's 'appease the tax for me' is that kind of request.

keyTerms.meaning: You are saying (a challenge to how the other person read the case)

steps.whatToRemember: Asking a גוי to act in your place makes his payment yours, and that is forbidden. Asking him only to save you from the tax is permitted, and that is what רב meant.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common idea: the exact wording of a request decides whether the other person counts as your agent.

phrases.english: Rav said to him:
Are you comparing it to "Go in my place to the tax collector"?
This case is only comparable to that one:
phrases.notes: "This" is רב's own case; "that" is the next line of the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: "But he may say to him: Save me from the tax collector."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases using the ברייתא's own second clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any request to a גוי to handle the wine tax is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'in my place', which makes the גוי an agent, is forbidden. 'Save me' is permitted, and רב's case is like that.

steps.title: New משנה: when the money from wine sold to a gentile is permitted
steps.stepSummary: If the price was fixed before the wine was measured out, the money is permitted. If the wine was measured out before the price was fixed, the money is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew who sells his wine to a gentile: if he set the price before measuring, the money is permitted. If he measured before setting the price, the money is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It deals with a Jew selling wine to a נכרי, and asks when the money he receives is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wine is poured into the גוי's vessel, it becomes forbidden as יין נסך. If the price was already set, the money was owed for permitted wine, so it is fine. If the price was set only afterward, the Jew is being paid for wine that is already forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Measured (the wine into the buyer's vessel)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the גמרא is built on this question: at what moment does the wine stop being the Jew's?

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who sells his wine to a gentile,
if he fixed the price before he measured it,
phrases.notes: Measuring here means pouring the wine into the gentile's vessel. That is the moment it becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: the money for it is permitted.
If he measured before he fixed the price,
the money for it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It continues the theme of earlier steps: a Jew must not take money that is payment for יין נסך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Price fixed before measuring means the money is permitted. Measuring before the price is fixed means the money is forbidden.

steps.title: אמימר: a gentile acquires by pulling
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that משיכה works as a way of acquiring for a גוי. His proof is that Persians send gifts to each other and never take them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: pulling acquires for a gentile. The proof is that Persians send gifts to each other and do not take them back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with אמימר's rule that a גוי can acquire an item by pulling it, even without paying. He supports this from Persian custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matters for the משנה, because it decides whether the wine already belongs to the גוי before it becomes forbidden. אמימר's evidence: Persian gifts become final once handed over, which shows the item has truly changed owners.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling, a way of acquiring movable items
Know that it is so (introduces a supporting proof)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ameimar said:
Pulling acquires in the case of a gentile.
Know that it is so,
for these Persians
send gifts to one another
and do not take them back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the question of acquisition that lies behind the משנה's timing rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי acquires movable items through משיכה.

steps.title: רב אשי: a gentile does not acquire by pulling
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees. He holds that משיכה does not acquire for a גוי, and says the Persians keep their gifts only out of pride.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: really, pulling does not acquire for a gentile. The Persians don't take back gifts only because pride stops them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with אמימר. He also knocks down אמימר's proof from the Persians.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי agrees that Persians don't retract gifts, but he gives a different reason. They avoid it because taking a gift back would be shameful, not because the law says the gift is acquired. So the custom proves nothing about acquisition.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, I will tell you (keeping my position)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not deny that Persians keep their gifts. He only denies that this proves a legal acquisition.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Actually, I will tell you,
pulling does not acquire in the case of a gentile.
And the fact that they do not take them back
is because haughtiness has taken hold of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אמימר's ruling and his proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both אמימר's ruling and the proof he brought from Persian gifts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Persian custom comes from social pride, not from legal acquisition.

steps.title: רב אשי's source: רב's advice to wine shopkeepers
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings support from רב. רב told shopkeepers to take payment before measuring wine for a גוי, and to lend the money first if needed, so they would never be paid for יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: where do I get this from? From what רב told the wine shopkeepers. When you measure wine for gentiles, take the money first and then measure. If they don't have money with them, lend it to them and take it back, so it becomes a loan they owe you. If you don't do this, the wine becomes forbidden while it is still yours, and the money you take is payment for forbidden wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a source for his view: practical advice that רב gave to wine sellers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was worried that the wine becomes forbidden while it still belongs to the Jewish seller. So he told the sellers to collect payment first. If the גוי has no cash, they should lend it to him so he pays it back, and what he owes is a loan rather than payment for יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: From where do I say this?
From what Rav said to those wine shopkeepers:
When you measure wine for gentiles,
take the money from them
and then measure for them.
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the word in round brackets. The better wording, in square brackets, simply means "measure."

phrases.english: And if they don't have money with them,
lend it to them and then take it from them,
so that it will be a loan they owe,
for if you don't do this,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא הָוֵי יֵין נֶסֶךְ — בִּרְשׁוּתַיְיכוּ קָא הָוֵי,
phrases.english: when it becomes libation wine, it becomes so while in your possession,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי שָׁקְילִתוּ דְּמֵי יֵין נֶסֶךְ קָא שָׁקְילִתוּ.
phrases.english: and when you take money, you are taking payment for libation wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אשי now backs up his view from step 9 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That משיכה does not acquire for a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's instruction to the wine shopkeepers to take payment before measuring.

steps.title: Setting up the inference: if pulling did acquire
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי begins showing why רב's advice proves his point: "If you think pulling acquires for a גוי..."
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it enters your mind that pulling acquires for a gentile...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב אשי is about to explain why רב's advice only makes sense if משיכה does not acquire for a גוי. The argument finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "if it enters your mind" brings up the opposing view in order to show a problem with it. The conclusion of the argument has not come yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (sets up an argument against a view)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that pulling acquires in the case of a gentile,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מְשִׁיכָה בְּגוֹי קוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts drawing the inference from רב's instruction in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That משיכה does not acquire for a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic of רב's advice, which the next lines will finish explaining.
